subject: Finovate POC — next steps, target metrics, and model options
messages:
From: Lucia Moreno <lucia@finovate.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alejandro Cruz <alejandro@finovate.io>, Finovate CSM <csm@finovate.io>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — POC goals and constraints

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap from Finovate's side and a couple of clarifying Qs so we can get a clean POC charter drafted.

Key priorities (from our product/ops):
- Multilingual support: Spanish (es-ES/LatAm) and Portuguese (pt-BR) for customer messaging flows.
- Low latency for interactive chat (goal: sub-300ms per token tail for user-facing path).
- Cost predictability during trial — we prefer a dedicated buffer for peak times.
- Strict data handling: retention 30 days, logs to be exported to our S3 with SSE-KMS.

Questions:
1) Which open models would you recommend for a ~2-week functional POC focusing on intent detection and short-response generation?
2) If we need to fall back to a higher-capacity model in outages, what does that look like operationally?

Attached: brief product notes from our PM (see references to the message templates).

Appreciate the draft charter — leaning on you to propose a concise acceptance criteria list.

—Lucia

[attachment: finovate-product-notes.docx (docx)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Moreno <lucia@finovate.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Alejandro Cruz <alejandro@finovate.io>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — POC goals and constraints

Hi Lucia — thanks for the clear lineup and for joining the call. Below is a proposed short POC charter and the recommended model options (open-model-first) + fallback plan. Please comment and we’ll turn this into a one-page SOW.

POC objective (2 weeks):
- Validate intent detection and templated response accuracy for English, Spanish, Portuguese in your customer messaging flows.
- Measure latency and cost under representative traffic (1–2 TPS steady, 5 TPS short bursts).

Success criteria (pass/fail thresholds):
- Intent accuracy >= 92% on the curated prompt set (weighted by high-volume intents).
- Response fidelity: < 2% critical hallucinations in the audit sample (annotated).
- Median generation latency (user-facing path) < 300ms for 95% of requests.
- End-to-end throughput support at 5 TPS with cold-starts under 1s for session init.

Recommended model shortlist (primary / secondary):
- Primary (cost-balanced, strong multilingual): Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized) — best latency/cost for short conversational turns.
- Secondary (higher-fidelity for tricky prompts): Llama-3-13B (int8) — slightly higher cost, stronger long-form coherence for edge cases.
- Fallback (capacity/availability): Falcon-40B-instruct (hosted dedicated pool) — used only if primary/secondary exceed SLOs or during planned failover windows.

Multilingual notes: both Mistral-Instruct-7B and Llama-3-13B show competent Spanish/Portuguese on the provided prompt set; we will allocate additional few-shot examples for pt-BR idioms in the eval set.

Evaluation plan & ownership:
- Prompt/eval set: Marissa to prepare (Marissa will lead annotator pass).
- Infra & routing: Vivek to provision dedicated burst pool and configure failover to Falcon-40B if latency spikes >500ms for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Data handling: Redwood will configure 30-day retention and S3 export per Finovate KMS keys (we’ll capture this in the SOW).

Timeline (proposed):
- Wed 17 Mar: Marissa sends first draft of eval prompts and golden-label guidelines.
- Thu 18 Mar: Vivek creates sandbox reserved capacity and shares dashboard link.
- Mon 22 Mar: POC start (14 calendar days).
- Mon 5 Apr: POC readout and acceptance decision.

Next steps / asks for Finovate:
- Please confirm target languages and any special dialect coverage beyond pt-BR/es-LatAm.
- Provide a list of ~50 high-volume intents/phrases (sample CSV) we should prioritize.

I’ve attached a short POC charter template — I’ll update it after your confirmation.

Thanks — Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Moreno <lucia@finovate.io>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Alejandro Cruz <alejandro@finovate.io>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finovate POC — next steps, target metrics, and model options

Great summary — I drafted an evaluation rubric and initial prompt sets attached. High-level notes: 

Evaluation rubric (what we'll measure automatically / manually):
- Intent classification F1 (automated) with business-critical intents weighted x2. Target F1 >= 0.90 (maps to ~92% accuracy threshold Priyom listed).
- Response appropriateness (manual sample): scale 1–5; accept if median >= 4.
- Hallucination rate (manual annotation on 200 samples): < 2% critical errors.
- Latency and token efficiency: per-route median latency target <300ms.

Prompt & test suite plan:
- Tier A: 50 high-volume templates (English + localized Spanish + pt-BR variants).
- Tier B: 30 edge-case prompts (longer context, ambiguous intents).
- Tier C: 20 stress templates for rate/cold-start profiling.

Model test matrix (what we'll run during POC):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: baseline tests for latency/cost.
- Llama-3-13B: accuracy-focused runs, include few-shot tuning.
- Falcon-40B-instruct: availability-only runs (limited queries) to validate fallback behavior.

Acceptance flow (how we declare success):
- Automated runs on Tier A/B pass thresholds -> readout with Finovate annotators.
- If a model fails a threshold, we capture root cause and recommend prompt tweaks or switch to secondary. No model switches without a documented rerun on the same prompt set.

Deliverables and owners: 
- eval-prompt-sets.csv (attached) — Marissa (owner).
- POC charter + SOW draft — Priyom (owner) + legal loop.
- Sandbox infra with routing and dashboard — Vivek (owner).

Action items:
- Finovate: share intent CSV and KMS key for S3 export by EOD Thu 18 Mar.
- Redwood: we will provision sandbox and share dashboard by Thu 18 Mar COB.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lucia Moreno <lucia@finovate.io>
Cc: Alejandro Cruz <alejandro@finovate.io>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finovate POC — infra readiness and routing notes

Quick ops note — provisioning update and a small ask on failover policy: 

Provisioning status:
- Reserved sandbox capacity: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs (burst pool + 1 hot replica) — configured.
- Routing policy: prefer primary model pool (Mistral-7B); on sustained latency > 500ms for 3m, route new sessions to Falcon-40B fallback pool.
- KV cache: enabled per-session to reduce repeated context costs; cache TTL 10m.

Failover detail:
- Fallback window will only route new sessions (not mid-session) to avoid token-in-flight inconsistencies. If Finovate prefers mid-session continuation, we can enable session migration but it requires warm KV-sync and ~1s stall.

Monitoring / dashboards:
- Shared dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/finovate/poc-FV-4821 (read-only link).
- Alerts: latency > 400ms (P1), error-rate > 2% (P1), cost burn > projected budget (P2).

Small ask for Finovate: confirm we can use the provided S3 endpoint and the KMS ARN for exported logs — I will not enable the export until we have a confirmed ARN.

I’ll kick off the sandbox and post credentials to the Drive folder.

—Vivek
Head of Ops, Redwood Inference
